EXECUTIVE SUMMARY
The past 24 hours have been dominated by the US-China summit in Beijing, where the Iran war and Strait of Hormuz were key discussion points, with the US attempting to pressure China to influence Tehran. Concurrently, highly contradictory reports emerged regarding alleged secret visits by Israeli Prime Minister Netanyahu and other top Israeli security officials to the UAE for coordination against Iran, which the UAE has officially denied. This highlights a complex interplay of public diplomacy, covert operations, and regional realignments surrounding the ongoing conflict.

IRAN
Military operations include IRGC forces simulating the downing of enemy helicopters and the IRGC aerospace commander delivering a supportive message to the national football team, framing it within a national struggle. Iran's Army affirmed it would not allow American munitions through the Strait of Hormuz, and the parliamentary commission finalized a plan for the security and development of the Persian Gulf and Strait of Hormuz, including legal incentives against US and Israeli leaders. The Representative of the Supreme Leader in the IRGC stated that no power could stand against Iran if it chose to act. Internally, Mohammad Abbasi was executed for the murder of a security officer during January riots. Economically, satellite imagery and TankerTrackers indicated a halt in crude oil exports from Kharg Island for several days, with storage tanks nearing capacity, suggesting significant economic pressure. Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi attended the BRICS meeting in India, where he declared Iran "invincible," warned against "foolish gambles" of enmity with Iran, and condemned Kuwait for an "unlawful" attack on an Iranian boat and the detention of four Iranian citizens. US Vice President Vance acknowledged "progress" in talks with Iran but noted it was unclear if it met President Trump's "red line" on nuclear weapons, while the US Secretary of Energy claimed Iran is close to nuclear weapons.

ISRAEL
The IDF continued military operations in southern Lebanon, striking over 40 Hezbollah sites, including weapon depots, rocket launchers, and terror infrastructure. In Gaza, the IDF killed Hamza Sharbasi, a Hamas Nukhba operative involved in the October 7 Nahal Oz raid, and Azzam al-Hayya, the son of Hamas’s chief negotiator, in an airstrike. An attempted ramming attack in the Etzion area of the West Bank was foiled. On the home front, false alarms were triggered in the Gaza envelope, and interceptors were launched at suspected aerial targets over southern Lebanon. Politically, Prime Minister Netanyahu's office confirmed a "secret visit" by him to the UAE, where he reportedly met Sheikh Mohamed bin Zayed, describing it as a "historic breakthrough," an assertion that was officially and unequivocally denied by the UAE Ministry of Foreign Affairs. Additionally, the Knesset dissolution bill was submitted by the coalition, and President Herzog called for a unity government after the upcoming elections. Israeli Chief of Staff Zamir stated in northern Samaria that "The campaign is not over, the IDF is ready to renew the fighting if required from Judea and Samaria to Tehran." Civilian impacts include Jerusalem Day events where over 200 Jews ascended the Temple Mount, some violating the status quo, and activists plan to monitor the Flag March for violence.

GAZA & WEST BANK
IDF operations in Gaza resulted in the killing of Hamas Nukhba operative Hamza Sharbasi and Azzam al-Hayya, son of a Hamas chief negotiator. In the West Bank, a ramming attack was thwarted in the Etzion area, and Israeli forces responded to violent unrest in Jaljulia (Area A) involving Israeli citizens who had entered the village after sheep theft from an illegal outpost, with reports of injured or killed individuals under investigation. Humanitarian concerns were raised by a human rights group reporting four Gaza doctors suffering starvation in Israeli prisons, and Israel reportedly destroyed dozens of Palestinian shops near Al-Quds to build an illegal settlement road. Hamas expressed readiness to hand over Gaza administration to a national committee upon full ceasefire implementation. Reports also indicated Israel had escalated bombing in Gaza since a ceasefire five weeks prior. Trucks carrying materials for "terror infrastructure" were observed entering Gaza.

LEBANON
Hezbollah launched an anti-tank guided missile and several mortars at Israeli troops in southern Lebanon, and also deployed multiple drones, some exploding near Israeli forces, with two reportedly shot down. Rockets were fired at Israeli troops near Zarit. Hezbollah claimed 17 operations on May 13, including drone strikes and targeting Israeli military vehicles and ambushing troops. UNIFIL headquarters in Naqoura sustained damage from "presumed" Hezbollah drone attacks on multiple occasions, with one unarmed, Iranian-made drone crashing on Sunday, and an armed fiber-optic drone crashing on May 5 without exploding. Israeli officials acknowledged Hezbollah's advanced drone capabilities were outmaneuvering their military. The IDF conducted over 40 strikes against Hezbollah infrastructure, including weapon depots and rocket launchers, in southern Lebanon. These strikes targeted locations such as Konin, Tabnin, al-Mansouri, Rumaish, Arabtzaalem, and Tyre, with multiple vehicle attacks reported near Beirut. At least 12 people, including two children, were killed in Israeli airstrikes on southern Lebanon. Lebanon officially filed a complaint with the UN Security Council, accusing Iran of "direct and overt interference" in its internal affairs and dragging the country into war.

SYRIA & IRAQ
Reports indicate Saudi Arabia and Kuwait reportedly conducted undeclared attacks against pro-Iranian militia targets in Iraq during the Iran war. Multiple explosions were heard in Erbil, Iraq, and Iranian-Kurdish opposition forces in northern Iraq were targeted by drone attacks, including a KDP-Iran radar on the Halabja mountains. Casualties were also reported from explosions in the Quneitra countryside and occupied Golan. Diplomatically, Syrian Foreign Minister Assad al-Shaibani expressed a desire for a comprehensive security agreement with Israel, contingent on Israel ceasing destabilizing actions, withdrawing all troops, and adhering to the 1974 disengagement agreement. Iraq's political parties are engaged in cabinet formation negotiations for Ali Al-Zaidi's government.

GULF STATES
The Israeli Prime Minister's Office claimed a "secret visit" by PM Netanyahu to the UAE, meeting Sheikh Mohamed bin Zayed, resulting in a "historic breakthrough," a claim officially and unequivocally denied by the UAE Ministry of Foreign Affairs. However, two senior UAE officials reportedly confirmed the visit, and both the head of Mossad, David Barnea, and the head of Shin Bet, David Zini, were reported to have made secret visits to the UAE for coordination. The UAE has begun installing anti-drone defenses around oil facilities near Dubai International Airport and confirmed the deployment of an Iron Dome system. An Emirati official stated the UAE prioritizes political solutions and negotiation, asserting that Arab-Iranian relations cannot be based on confrontation. Saudi Arabia and Kuwait reportedly conducted undeclared attacks against pro-Iranian militia targets in Iraq during the Iran war. The Economist reported that Gulf states have incurred tens of billions of dollars in costs, with Saudi oil exports down by one-third and UAE exports by half since the war began. Hapag-Lloyd, a shipping company, reported $50-60 million weekly in additional costs due to the Strait of Hormuz closure. US Secretary of State Rubio stated that China has an interest in condemning Iran's actions in the Strait of Hormuz due to global economic suffering affecting Chinese trade.

KEY DEVELOPMENTS
1.  **Secret Israeli-UAE High-Level Engagements**: Israeli PM Netanyahu's office confirmed a "secret visit" to the UAE to meet Sheikh Mohamed bin Zayed, calling it a "historic breakthrough," which the UAE Ministry of Foreign Affairs officially denied. Mossad chief Barnea and Shin Bet head Zini were also reported to have made secret visits for coordination.
2.  **US-China Summit Discussions on Iran**: US President Trump met Chinese President Xi Jinping in Beijing, with a key focus on persuading China to pressure Iran regarding the Strait of Hormuz. US VP Vance indicated "progress" in talks with Iran, while China is reportedly reluctant to reduce economic support or stop dual-use goods.
3.  **Intensified Israel-Hezbollah Confrontations**: The IDF struck over 40 Hezbollah sites in southern Lebanon, while Hezbollah claimed 17 operations including drone strikes and rocket attacks that damaged UNIFIL headquarters in Naqoura. Israel intercepted multiple aerial threats.
4.  **Iran's Economic Stress and Execution**: Iran executed Mohammad Abbasi for murder, and satellite imagery along with TankerTrackers data indicated a halt in oil exports from Kharg Island for several days, with storage tanks nearing capacity.
5.  **Strait of Hormuz Blockade and Economic Impact**: US CENTCOM reported diverting 67 commercial vessels and disrupting four as part of its blockade. The IEA stated oil supply losses from the Strait's closure amounted to 12.8 million barrels per day since February.
6.  **Lebanese UN Complaint Against Iran**: Lebanon filed an official complaint with the UN Security Council, accusing Iran of "direct and overt interference" in its internal affairs and pushing it into war.
7.  **IDF Readiness for Broader Conflict**: Israeli Chief of Staff Zamir declared the IDF is prepared to renew fighting "from Judea and Samaria to Tehran."
8.  **China Leveraging Iran War**: A classified US intelligence report indicated China gained diplomatic, economic, military, and intelligence advantages from the Iran war, portraying the US as a destabilizing force.
9.  **Reported Saudi/Kuwaiti Strikes in Iraq**: Sources indicated Saudi Arabia and Kuwait conducted undeclared attacks against pro-Iranian militia targets in Iraq during the Iran war.

THREAT ASSESSMENT
Escalation risks remain high due to continued direct and proxy confrontations, particularly between Israel and Hezbollah, alongside Lebanon's formal complaint against Iran, escalating diplomatic tensions. Chief of Staff Zamir's explicit statement of IDF readiness for conflict extending to Tehran underscores the potential for wider regional engagement. Active flashpoints include southern Lebanon, the Strait of Hormuz (where the US maintains a naval blockade), and northern Iraq, which has seen strikes against Iranian-Kurdish opposition groups and alleged Saudi/Kuwaiti attacks on pro-Iranian militias. Military postures reflect ongoing conflict, with the IDF continuing offensive strikes in Lebanon, the UAE fortifying its oil infrastructure against drone attacks, and the US maintaining its naval presence. The US "red line" on Iran's nuclear program remains a critical threshold, while Iran views foreign interference and attacks as unacceptable, contributing to a volatile environment.

REGIONAL & INTERNATIONAL RESPONSE
The US posture is marked by diplomatic engagement with China to pressure Iran, with VP Vance noting "progress" in talks but reiterating the nuclear "red line." CENTCOM continues its Hormuz blockade, while the Pentagon is ordering new cruise missiles due to depleted stockpiles. The US Senate rejected a resolution to end the war with Iran for the seventh time. Gulf states exhibit a complex response: the UAE officially denied Israeli PM Netanyahu's reported visit, emphasized political solutions, and is installing anti-drone defenses; Saudi Arabia and Kuwait are reported to have attacked pro-Iranian militias in Iraq; and Gulf state foreign ministers are discussing the Hormuz situation. China, during President Xi's meeting with US President Trump, discussed Iran and the Strait of Hormuz, though Reuters reports China's reluctance to curb economic support for Iran. A classified US intelligence report indicated China has leveraged the Iran war to its advantage. Italy plans to send minesweepers to the Gulf, indicating European concern over maritime security.

INTELLIGENCE NOTES
Significant contradictions exist regarding Israeli PM Netanyahu's alleged "secret visit" to the UAE; the Israeli PMO confirmed it as a "historic breakthrough," while the UAE Ministry of Foreign Affairs issued an official and unequivocal denial. However, two senior UAE officials reportedly confirmed the visit, complicating the assessment. Unverified claims include a reported CIA raid on Tulsi Gabbard's office (denied by her spokesperson), discussions by Chinese companies to sell arms to Iran via third countries (based on classified US intelligence), and President Trump's alleged assassination instructions to Vice President Vance. Propaganda indicators are evident in Iran's Foreign Minister's rhetoric at BRICS, Press TV's framing of the conflict, and the IRGC's efforts to link national sports with military struggle. Reporting gaps persist concerning the precise nature of "progress" in US-Iran talks, the full details of Iran's oil export halt, and independent verification of casualties from IDF actions in the West Bank.
